chunks: I enjoin upon you fear of Allāh
Who has left no excuse against what He has warned, has exhausted argument (of guidance) about the (right) path He has shown.
He has warned you of the enemy that steals into hearts and stealthily speaks into ears,
and thereby misguides and brings about destruction, makes (false) promises and keeps under wrong impression; He represents evil sins in attractive shape, and shows as light even serious crimes.
When he has deceived his comrades and exhausted the pledge
he begins to find fault with what he presented as good, and considers serious what he had shown as light, and threatens from what he had shown as safe.
ai.seo_question: How does Satan deceive humans according to Imam Ali's sermon in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from the Al-Gharra highlights the psychological mechanism of *istidraj* (gradual ensnarement), where Satan initially minimizes major sins to lull believers into complacency before revealing their true severity. In Shia exegesis, this serves as a critical warning against the subtle erosion of faith through incremental moral compromise, emphasizing that divine warning was already sufficient for accountability.
